scope_note: Canadian evaluation material for deterministic legal-text tooling: typed-anchor extraction and structural parsing. No model API was used to build, select, classify or annotate anything here. CanLII was not accessed.

files.registry.jsonl: 33 rows, one JSON object per artifact. Rights recorded PER ARTIFACT, not per repository.
files.anchor-forms.jsonl: 60 hand-collected Canadian anchor surface forms, each offset-verified against a corpus file.
files.structure-gold/statutes/<slug>.structure: Provider-native section map + derived raw-text spans.
files.structure-gold/decisions/<slug>.structur: Paragraph markers with spine/quoted roles + provider-native citation list.
files.external/canlegalragbench/queries.jsonl: 532 MIT-licensed CanLegalRAGBench query/answer annotations (no source document text).

zero_annotation_trick.statutes: A2AJ ships unofficial_sections_en (JSON string: section label -> section body) ALONGSIDE the raw text unofficial_text_en. The section map is produced independently of the raw text, so it is gold for a text-only skeleton parser with no human annotation. structure_provenance = 'provider-native'.
zero_annotation_trick.decisions: No native section field exists for case law. Two other native signals are used: (1) the paragraph numbers the court itself published inline, e.g. '[47]', located by regex; (2) A2AJ's provider-native cases_cited_en neutral-citation list. structure_provenance = 'derived-from-native-markers' and every record carries a structure_derivation block stating the exact rule.

provenance.upstream_license: full upstream licence string from the row

structure_derivation.raw_span: derived: label located by line-anchored heading match, disambiguated by verifying the native body follows; span ends at the next located heading
structure_derivation.warning: the provider's section-map key order is NOT document order for decimal labels; use doc_order

sections.label: string, e.g. '231', '83.01', '25-49', 'Schedule'
sections.map_order: int, index in the provider's section map
sections.doc_order: int|null, index in raw-text reading order

decision_structure_json.name: style of cause
decision_structure_json.provenance: same shape as statutes, with source=huggingface:a2aj/canadian-case-law, file=NSCA/train.parquet, field_structure=(none: paragraph numbers are inline)

structure_derivation.rule: regex ^[ \t]*\[(\d+)\] in MULTILINE mode over the verbatim raw text
structure_derivation.role_rule: walk markers in document order with expected=1; marker is 'spine' iff int(label)==expected (then expected+=1), else 'quoted_or_foreign'
structure_derivation.note: bracketed numbers are the court's own published paragraph numbers; the only derivation is locating them and separating the decision's own sequence from paragraph numbers inside block quotations of other judgments

structure.quoted_count: int, quoted-judgment paragraph numbers + inline footnote refs

native_citations.description: Neutral citations A2AJ detected, in order of first appearance, self-citations excluded. NEUTRAL CITATIONS ONLY: traditional reporter citations such as '[1999] 3 S.C.R. 423' are NOT captured.

anchor_forms_jsonl.surface_text: string, verbatim from the source file
anchor_forms_jsonl.note: why this form matters / what breaks on it
anchor_forms_jsonl.char_offset: int, exact offset of surface_text in source_file
anchor_forms_jsonl.context: +-90 chars around the match, newlines flattened

how_to_score.principle: Run the text-only skeleton parser over <slug>.txt and compare against <slug>.structure.json. Match on LABELS, not on body text.

statutes_and_regulations.gold_label_set: G = {s.label for s in structure.sections if s.anchored}. Unanchored labels have no heading in the raw text, so including them is an unfair denominator; report them separately.
statutes_and_regulations.label_metrics: precision / recall / F1 of the parser's emitted labels P against G, matching on the label STRING. Never normalise decimal labels to floats: '83.01' != '83.1'.
statutes_and_regulations.order_metric: compare the parser's emitted sequence against structure.labels_doc_order (exact-sequence match or Kendall tau). Scoring against labels_map_order is a BUG: map_order_equals_doc_order is false for the Criminal Code and IRPA.
statutes_and_regulations.span_metric: optional. For labels in G intersect P, character-interval IoU of the parser span against section.raw_span. raw_span runs heading-to-next-heading and therefore INCLUDES interleaved '### marginal note' headings; a parser that strips them will under-cover. Report span score separately from label score.
statutes_and_regulations.range_collapsed: labels with anchor_kind == 'range-collapsed' share one heading (e.g. '**157 and 158**' covers labels '157' and '158'). Score these separately; a parser emitting only '157' is partially right.
statutes_and_regulations.do_not: Do NOT score against section.body directly. The provider strips the label from the body and drops interleaved marginal-note headings, so the native body is NOT a contiguous substring of the raw text.

decisions.spine_detection: Compare the parser's paragraph labels against structure.labels_spine (685 real paragraphs across the 8 decisions). Emitting any of the 375 quoted_or_foreign markers counts as a FALSE POSITIVE. This is the metric that matters: a parser scoring well on labels_all_markers but poorly on labels_spine is doing regex matching, not structural parsing.
decisions.citation_extraction: Compare extracted neutral citations against native_citations.values (242 across the 8 decisions). Score RECALL against the native list. Score PRECISION only over neutral-citation-shaped extractions, because A2AJ extracts neutral citations ONLY: traditional reporter citations are absent from the gold and must NOT be counted as false positives.
decisions.independent_check: Every spine is exactly 1..n and each ends on a genuine disposition paragraph, which is how the role rule was validated.

structural_traps_encoded.trap: section-map key order is not document order
structural_traps_encoded.detail: For decimal labels A2AJ sorts 83.01, 83.1, 83.02, 83.2, 83.03, 83.3 ... because '01' and '1' collide in its sort key. A cursor-based forward scan over map order silently drops ~59% of Criminal Code sections.
The map has separate keys '157' and '158' but the raw text has a single heading '**157 and 158** [Repealed, R.S., 1985, c. 19 (3rd Supp.), s. 2]'.

structural_traps_encoded.trap: section map is a superset of the raw text
structural_traps_encoded.detail: 250 of 2848 labels never appear as a heading: repealed sections, '[blank]' placeholders, '[Amendments]', and 'Omitted (amends or repeals other Acts)'.

2026 NSCA 36 contains 231 '[N]' tokens but only 119 real paragraphs. The rest are paragraph numbers inside block quotations of OTHER judgments and inline footnote references such as 'offences.[1]'. Line position alone is insufficient; sequence continuity is required.

declared_gaps: SBC / RSBC (British Columbia) citation forms: excluded because all 574 LEGISLATION-BC rows have a NULL upstream_license, so rights are unknown.

C.R.C., c. 870 (Consolidated Regulations of Canada): REGULATIONS-FED is 103.7 MB, over the per-download budget. An example exists in the Beaver fixtures at backend/src/lib/__tests__/fixtures/sourcedoc/a2aj-regs-fed-crc870-a01.json.
CARSWELLNAT database citations and Quebec RLRQ forms: observed in external/canlegalragbench/queries.jsonl but outside slice (a)'s texts, so no offset-verified entry was recorded.
French-language documents: corpus is English-only, so 'L.R.C. (1985), ch. C-46' and 'art.' pinpoints are unrepresented. A2AJ carries *_fr fields for the same rows, so this is cheap to add later.

reproducing: raw_text_sha256 in each .structure.json (and in registry.jsonl) pins the exact text. To re-pull an artifact, read its registry row and fetch path_in_source at revision from source_url. Bulk parquet files were held only in a scratch directory and are NOT part of this corpus; only the 18 selected documents and one MIT-licensed annotation file were copied in.
